three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.evidence: a traced time.sleep stack showed two complete probe sandboxes inside a single run_staged_confined_command call
three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.fix_1: namespace_primitives_cheap() -- a shutil.which check over the seven required binaries, memoised per uid/gid, 0.2 ms. It can only REFUSE faster; it never returns True as a substitute for the probe.
three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.fix_2: the availability answer is now fetched once per call and reused
three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.security_note: this does not weaken the probe. If a primitive is missing the answer is False in 0.2 ms instead of after a wasted sandbox; if all are present the real probe still runs and still decides.

three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.evidence: 0.455 s of a 0.601 s five-run profile was three time.sleep calls inside subprocess._wait
three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.fix: a blocking wait plus a threading.Timer that kills the process group at the deadline -- the same guarantee the polling loop was approximating, with no sleep at all
three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.verified_by: test_the_timeout_still_fires_without_polling -- a /usr/bin/sleep 30 under wallclock_s=1 returns WALLCLOCK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED in under 5 s

three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.evidence: after both fixes the profile shows posix.waitpid as the dominant cost -- the parent is now genuinely blocked on the child, not sleeping
three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.what_the_child_spends_it_on: the _SETUP bash script performs nine mount operations (rprivate, tmpfs, bind, remount ro, four /usr /bin /lib /lib64 binds, device binds). Measured by running _SETUP directly against /bin/true: 53-62 ms.
three_wastes_found_by_profiling_none_of_.conclusion: 55 ms is the floor of THIS design. It is not fixable by micro-optimisation.

the_honest_gap_to_the_frontier.what_gets_this_tree_under_55ms: a long-lived pre-mounted sandbox handed out per command, or a pre-warmed fork of the mounted namespace. The tree already has a zygote worker pool (canonical/swe_kernel/zygote_worker_pool_v1.py); the carrier is not in it. That is a design change, not a bug fix.
the_honest_gap_to_the_frontier.what_i_did_NOT_do: I did not skip the workspace manifest, and I did not skip the probe's real sandbox. Both would have made the number smaller and the invariant unverified while still reporting it.

the_larger_remaining_cost_this_round_did.problem: the workspace manifest walks the whole tree: 235 ms for 1 file, 1267 ms for the 16k-file repository root
the_larger_remaining_cost_this_round_did.why_it_matters: any command carried with the repo as workspace pays a full-tree walk
the_larger_remaining_cost_this_round_did.frontier_answer_found: incremental content-addressed verification -- read only the tiles that changed rather than re-hashing the whole history (tlog-tiles / Merkle tile layouts, 2026). Measured elsewhere in the same design family: an incremental verify after N appended records reads O(changed tiles), not O(entire history).
the_larger_remaining_cost_this_round_did.not_done_because: it changes what 'the live tree is untouched' MEANS, from a full comparison to a proof about a delta. That is a governance decision about the strength of the invariant, not a performance patch, and it is the next round's work rather than this one's.
